chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The least of what suffices you from supplication after the obligatory prayer is that you should say: 'O Allah, I ask You of every good of which Your Knowledge has encompassed, and I seek refuge with You from every evil of which Your Knowledge has encompassed. O Allah, I ask You for Your well-being in all my affairs, and I seek refuge with You from the disgrace of the world and the punishment of the Hereafter.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite after the obligatory prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi through the chain of Zurarah, a key companion of Imam al-Baqir, this supplication serves as a comprehensive post-prayer du'a encapsulating the essence of divine mercy and protection. It reflects the Shia emphasis on seeking 'afiyah' (comprehensive well-being) and aligns with the Prophetic tradition of concluding obligatory prayers with remembrance, reinforcing the spiritual continuity between ritual worship and daily life.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The least of what would suffice you from the supplication after the Obligatory (Salāt) is that you should be saying, ‘O Allahazwj! I ask Youazwj of every goodness encompassed by Yourazwj Knowledge, and I seek Refuge with Youazwj from every evil encompassed by Yourazwj Knowledge. O Allahazwj! I ask Youazwj of Yourazwj Granting good health in my affairs, all of them, and I seek Refuge with Youazwj from the disgrace of the world and the Punishment of the Hereafter’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

The least that you should say after an obligatory Salah (prayer) is to say, ‘O Lord, I ask from You of all good which Your knowledge has encompassed, and seek refuge with You against every evil thing that Your knowledge has encompassed. O Lord, I ask from You good health in all of my affairs and I seek refuge with You against failures in this life and torment in the next life.’”
